cases.evidence_note: Per diem payments of $160,600 (box 1, per diem checked, qualified contract) for 365 days, care costs $120,000, no reimbursements. Line 21 = $420 × 365 = $153,300; line 23 the larger, $153,300; line 25 $153,300; line 26 = $160,600 − $153,300 = $7,300, on Schedule 1 line 8e.
As x2s1o.f8853c.per_diem_excess with care costs of $158,000: line 23 takes line 22, $158,000; line 26 = $160,600 − $158,000 = $2,600.
Per diem payments of $100,000 for 365 days, no costs entered: line 26 = $100,000 − $153,300, floored at zero.
Per diem payments of $160,600 for 365 days, no costs, $10,000 of reimbursements for care in the period: line 25 = $153,300 − $10,000 = $143,300; line 26 = $17,300.
Accelerated death benefits of $20,000 paid at a set rate for 30 days while chronically ill (line 19), no long-term care per diem: line 20 $20,000, line 21 = $420 × 30 = $12,600, line 26 = $7,400.
Payments that only repaid costs (no per diem): nothing taxable, line 26 zero; the Section C amounts are not asked.
Someone else also received periodic payments for the same insured (line 15 Yes): refused at line 26 (Multiple Payees). The refused values are the evaluator's.

f8853c[p0].line26.remedy: When someone else also received payments at a set rate for the same insured person, the $420-a-day limit is figured for everyone together on an attached statement; that is outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 9, Multiple Payees, "attach a statement duplicating lines 18 through 26"
cite.revision: 2025 (the revision for tax year 2025, archived from irs-prior after irs.gov posted a later revision)

cases.evidence_note: The payment rate changed in 2025 (more than one LTC period): refused at line 26. The refused values are the evaluator's.

f8853c[p0].line26.form: Form 8853, Section C (more than one LTC period)
f8853c[p0].line26.remedy: Payments at more than one rate in 2025 make more than one long-term care period, each figured on its own Section C; that is outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 8, Line 18, "If you have more than one LTC period, you must separately calculate the taxable amount of the payments received during each LTC period"
cite.revision: 2025 (the revision for tax year 2025, archived from irs-prior after irs.gov posted a later revision)

cases.evidence_note: Per diem payments under a contract that is not a qualified LTC insurance contract: refused at line 26 (line 17 caution). The refused values are the evaluator's.

f8853c[p0].line26.form: Form 8853, Section C, line 17 (a contract that is not a qualified LTC insurance contract)
f8853c[p0].line26.remedy: Payments at a set rate under a contract that is not a qualified long-term care insurance contract are taxable only to the extent they are not excludable, figured outside Form 8853; that is outside this tool.

cite.locator: Form 8853 (2025), line 17, Caution, "Don’t use lines 18 through 26 to figure the taxable amount of benefits paid under an LTC insurance contract that isn’t a qualified LTC insurance contract"
cite.revision: 2025; created 2025-03-27 (the revision for tax year 2025, archived from irs-prior after irs.gov posted a later revision)

cases.evidence_note: Reimbursements under a contract issued before August 1, 1996: refused at line 25. The refused values are the evaluator's.

f8853c[p0].line25.form: Form 8853, line 24 (reimbursements under a contract issued before August 1, 1996)
f8853c[p0].line25.remedy: Reimbursements under a long-term care contract issued before August 1, 1996, are generally left off line 24 unless the contract was later changed; that is outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 9, Line 24, "Generally, don’t include on line 24 reimbursements for qualified LTC services you received under a contract issued before August 1, 1996"
cite.revision: 2025 (the revision for tax year 2025, archived from irs-prior after irs.gov posted a later revision)
